prompt: Complete Grid.render, which builds a text grid by asking a BiFunction<Integer, Integer, String> for each cell, joining cells with spaces and rows with newlines.
explanation: BiFunction<Integer, Integer, String> is a functional interface whose apply method takes two arguments and returns a result, so callers can plug in any rule for what a cell contains. render stays completely generic: it only owns the layout (spaces between cells, newlines between rows) and delegates the content decision to the function it was handed. Appending separators before each element except the first is a clean way to avoid trailing spaces and newlines.
hints: Use two nested for loops, r over rows and c over cols, and get each cell with cell.apply(r, c).
Build the result in a StringBuilder rather than concatenating strings in the loop.
To avoid trailing separators, append " " only when c > 0 and "\n" only when r > 0.
